findings.summary: Neil's Arc indexer stays three blocks behind the head. The integration cursor supports that margin, but the API indexer never sets it, so a lagging eth_getLogs response can advance the cursor past logs it did not return.

evidence: commerce/api/src/indexer.ts:14-18 adds confirmations, default 0, and line 67 passes it to LogCursor
commerce/api/src/server.ts:109 sets confirmations to 3n when CHAIN_MODE is arc, else 0n
commerce/sdk/src/chain/cursor.ts:66-70 computes safe as head minus confirmations and returns before getLogs when safe is behind the cursor
commerce/sdk/src/chain/cursor.ts:77-89 calls getLogs through safe and then saves that block
commerce/api/src/indexer.ts:107 persists the saved block even when the window contains no events
commerce/api/src/server.ts:101-105 starts the indexer with only db, chain, and cursorStart

effect: commerce/api/src/market.ts:175-188 returns the latest indexed core status and calls live getJob only when no indexed status exists. A skipped later event leaves an older indexed status in place.
commerce/api/src/market.ts:691-727 reads ProofAccepted and KeyReleased only from the events table. It does not fall back to the chain for submitTx, envelopeHash, keyCommitment, releaseTx, or key.
commerce/api/src/market.ts:559-601 links funding from the named transaction receipt and, in arc mode, a snapshot at that receipt block. That path does not use the indexer.
findings.minimalPort: Add an optional confirmations field to IndexerOptions and pass it to LogCursor, leaving the default at 0n so current callers stay unchanged. In server.ts, pass 3n when chain.mode is arc. Use the existing ApiChain mode. Do not add CHAIN_MODE, do not change funding-receipt, and do not change worker or signer policy.
